title: MANAGING OFFENCES
mv: Now I urge you, brethren, note those who cause divisions and offenses, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and avoid them.
mvp: “Now I urge you, brethren, note those who cause divisions and offenses, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and avoid them.” Romans 16:17 (NKJV)
assignment: List five (5) practical actions you will take this week to manage offences (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Offence is a lack of good manners, disregard for others, wounding the feelings of others, etc. Offences are part of human relationships. Jesus already warned that “offences will surely come” (Luke 17:1a). In the church, like other circles, offences may arise through words, attitudes, neglect, or misunderstandings. If not properly managed, offences can lead to bitterness, division, and even backsliding. However, God expects believers to handle offences with maturity, love, and forgiveness so that unity in the church and other circles is preserved.

Offences are inevitable; even among believers, misunderstanding is bound to occur (Luke 17:1; Matthew 18:7). The sources of offences include careless words or actions (James 3:2), unmet expectations (2 Timothy 4:16), pride, envy, and selfishness (3 John 9-10). The danger of offences includes bitterness and strife (Hebrews 12:15), spiritual wavering (Matthew 24:10), and hindered prayers (Mark 11:25-26).

The Bible outline various ways to handle offences: Personal approach, that is, speaking directly with the person, not gossip about it (Matthew 18:15); The witness approach, if unresolved, involve one or two mature believers as witnesses (Matthew 18:16); The Church approach, if still unresolved, escalate it to church leadership for intervention (Matthew 18:17); Forgiveness must be part of our lifestyle (Matthew 18:21-22; Colossians 3:13); Let love rule because it covers a multitude of sins (1 Peter 4:8); Choose reconciliation over retaliation (Romans 12:17-19).
Other practical ways Believers can manage offences include:

i: Guard Your Heart, do not allow bitterness to take root (Proverbs 4:23).
Be Quick to Listen, Slow to Speak, many offences can be prevented by careful communication (James 1:19).
Avoid Being a Source of Offence, Live sensitively so others are not made to stumble (Romans 14:13; 1 Corinthians 8:9).
Seek Peace, Pursue peace with all men, as much as lies in you (Hebrews 12:14; Romans 12:18).
Pray for Grace, Pray for those who offend you; ask God for strength to forgive (Philippians 4:6-7).

b.x: Offences are inevitable, but how we respond determines whether we grow or stumble.
